units.zh: 朱瑄，宋州下邑人也。
units.en: Zhu Xuan came from Xiayi in Songzhou.
units.literal: Zhu Xuan was a native of Xiayi in Song prefecture.

units.zh: 父慶，里之豪右，以攻剽販鹽為事，吏捕之伏法。
units.en: His father Qing, a village strongman, lived by banditry and salt-running until the authorities caught and executed him.
units.literal: His father Qing was a local magnate who made his living by raiding and smuggling salt; officials seized him and he was executed by law.

units.zh: 瑄坐父罪以笞免。
units.en: Xuan was caned and dismissed because of his father's offense.
units.literal: Xuan, implicated in his father's crime, was flogged and released.

units.zh: 因入王敬武軍為小校。
units.en: He then joined Wang Jingwu's forces as a low-ranking officer.
units.literal: Thereupon he entered Wang Jingwu's army as a junior officer.

units.zh: 唐中和二年，諫議大夫張浚征兵於青州，敬武遣將曹全晸率軍赴之，以瑄隸焉。
units.en: In Tang Zhonghe year 2, Censor Zhang Jun mustered troops at Qingzhou; Jingwu dispatched Cao Quanzhen's army to answer the call, and Xuan went with it.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe of Tang, Remonstrance Censor Zhang Jun raised troops at Qingzhou; Jingwu sent the general Cao Quanzhen with an army to join him, with Xuan attached to that force.

units.zh: 以戰功累遷列校。
units.en: Repeated victories raised him through the ranks of field officers.
units.literal: Through battle merit he was repeatedly promoted among the column commanders.

units.zh: 賊敗出關，全晸以本軍還鎮。
units.en: After the rebels broke and fled beyond the passes, Quanzhen marched his own troops back to their post.
units.literal: When the rebels were defeated and driven out of the passes, Quanzhen returned to garrison with his original army.

units.zh: 會鄆帥薛崇卒，部將崔君預據城叛，全晸攻之，殺君預自為留後。
units.en: Yan commander Xue Chong died; his subordinate Cui Junyu rebelled and held the city. Quanzhen stormed it, killed Junyu, and declared himself acting commissioner.
units.literal: When Yan military commissioner Xue Chong died, his officer Cui Junyu seized the city in revolt; Quanzhen attacked, killed Junyu, and made himself acting commissioner.

units.zh: 瑄以功授濮州刺史、鄆州馬步軍都將。
units.en: For his service Xuan received Pu prefecture and command of Yanzhou's combined cavalry and infantry.
units.literal: Xuan, for merit, was appointed prefect of Pu and commander of Yan's horse-and-foot forces.

units.zh: 光啟初，魏博韓允中攻鄆，全晸為其所害。
units.en: Early in the Guangqi reign Han Yunzhong of Weibo attacked Yan, and Quanzhen fell in the fighting.
units.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, Weibo's Han Yunzhong attacked Yan; Quanzhen was killed by him.

units.zh: 瑄據城自固。
units.en: Xuan barricaded himself inside the city.
units.literal: Xuan held the city and fortified himself.

units.zh: 三軍推為留後。
units.en: The army proclaimed him acting commissioner.
units.literal: The three armies pushed him to be acting commissioner.

units.zh: 允中敗，朝廷以瑄為天平軍節度使，累加官至檢校太尉、同平章事。
units.en: After Yunzhong's defeat the throne appointed Xuan commissioner of Tianping; he eventually reached honorary Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.
units.literal: When Yunzhong was defeated, the court made Xuan military commissioner of Tianping, and he rose in rank to honorary Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.

units.zh: 太祖初鎮大梁，兵威未振，連歲為秦宗權所圍，士不解甲，危殆日數四。
units.en: When the Founder first governed Daliang his power was still weak; Qin Zongquan besieged him year after year, troops never out of mail, danger threatening several times daily.
units.literal: When the Founder first held Daliang, his military prestige was not yet established; year after year he was besieged by Qin Zongquan, his men never doffing armor, peril coming several times a day.

units.zh: 太祖以瑄同宗，早兄事之，乃遣使求援於瑄。
units.en: Calling Xuan kin, the Founder had long treated him as an elder brother and now begged him for help.
units.literal: The Founder, treating Xuan as a clansman, had long addressed him as elder brother, and sent envoys to seek aid from Xuan.

units.zh: 光啟末，宗權急攻大梁，瑄與弟瑾率兗、鄆之師來援，大敗蔡賊，解圍而遁。
units.en: Late in Guangqi, Zongquan hammered Daliang; Xuan and Jin marched troops from Yan and Yanzhou, crushed the Cai army, broke the siege, and retired.
units.literal: At the end of Guangqi, Zongquan pressed the attack on Daliang; Xuan and his younger brother Jin led Yan and Yanzhou forces to the rescue, routed the Cai rebels, lifted the siege, and withdrew.

units.zh: 太祖感其力，厚禮以歸之。
units.en: Grateful for the rescue, the Founder honored them lavishly on their departure.
units.literal: The Founder, grateful for their effort, sent them home with rich courtesy.

units.zh: 先是，瑄、瑾駐於大梁，睹太祖軍士驍勇，私心愛之。
units.en: While stationed at Daliang, Xuan and Jin had seen how fierce the Founder's troops were and coveted them.
units.literal: Earlier, while Xuan and Jin were encamped at Daliang, they saw the Founder's soldiers were fierce, and secretly admired them.

units.zh: 及歸，厚懸金帛於界上以誘焉。
units.en: Back home they posted rich bounties of gold and silk along the frontier to lure deserters.
units.literal: On returning home they hung out heavy rewards of gold and silk on the border to entice them.

units.zh: 諸軍貪其厚利，私遁者甚眾。
units.en: Many of the Founder's men slipped away for the generous pay.
units.literal: The various armies, greedy for the rich profit, deserted in great numbers.

units.zh: 太祖移牒以讓之，瑄來詞不遜，由是始構隙焉。
units.en: The Founder rebuked him in writing; Xuan answered rudely, and enmity began.
units.literal: The Founder sent a written protest; Xuan came with insolent words, and from this the rift began.

units.zh: 及秦宗權敗，太祖移軍攻時溥於徐州。
units.en: After Zongquan's fall the Founder turned his armies on Shi Pu at Xuzhou.
units.literal: When Qin Zongquan was defeated, the Founder shifted his army to attack Shi Pu at Xuzhou.

units.zh: 時瑄方右溥，乃遣使來告太祖曰：「巢、權繼為蛇虺，毒螫中原，與君把臂同盟，輔車相依。
units.en: Xuan was then siding with Pu and wrote the Founder: "Chao and Zongquan were serpents in turn, stinging the heartland; we clasped arms as allies, dependent as chariot wheels.
units.literal: At that time Xuan was backing Pu, and sent an envoy to tell the Founder: "Huang Chao and Zongquan in succession were vipers, poisoning the Central Plain; you and I clasped arms in alliance, cheek by jowl as in a chariot.

units.zh: 今賊已平殄，人粗聊生，吾弟宜念遠圖，不可自相魚肉。
units.en: The rebels are gone and men barely survive; brother, keep the larger design—do not devour each other.
units.literal: Now the bandits are wiped out and people barely live again; my younger brother should think of the long view and not tear one another apart like fish and flesh.

units.zh: 或行人之失辭，疆吏之逾法，可以理遣，未得便睽和好。
units.en: A courier's slip or a frontier officer's breach can be reasoned away; do not break our bond lightly.
units.literal: Perhaps a traveler's loose word or a border officer's excess may be settled by reason; you must not lightly break the good understanding.

units.zh: 投鼠忌器，弟幸思之。」
units.en: Strike the rat but spare the vessel—brother, weigh that."
units.literal: When casting at a rat, one fears the vessel—brother, think on this."

units.zh: 太祖方怒時溥通於孫儒，不從其言。
units.en: The Founder, furious that Pu was colluding with Sun Ru, ignored the plea.
units.literal: The Founder was then angry that Pu was in league with Sun Ru and did not heed his words.

units.zh: 及龐師古攻徐州，瑄出師來援，太祖深銜之。
units.en: When Pang Shigu besieged Xuzhou, Xuan came to Pu's aid, and the Founder never forgave it.
units.literal: When Pang Shigu attacked Xuzhou, Xuan marched out to aid Pu; the Founder deeply resented it.

units.zh: 徐既平，太祖並兵以攻鄆，自景福元年冬遣朱友裕領軍渡濟，至乾寧三年宿軍齊、鄆間，大小凡數十戰，語在《太祖紀》中。
units.en: Once Xuzhou fell he massed troops against Yan: from winter of Jingfu 1 Zhu Youyu crossed the Ji, and by Qianning 3 armies lay between Qi and Yan in dozens of clashes recorded in the 《Founder's Annals》.
units.literal: After Xu was pacified, the Founder united his forces to attack Yan; from winter of Jingfu year 1 he sent Zhu Youyu with an army across the Ji, until in Qianning year 3 he camped between Qi and Yan, fighting great and small battles several tens of times, as told in the 《Founder's Annals》.

units.zh: 自是野無人耕，屬城悉為我有。
units.en: Fields lay empty; every subordinate city fell to him.
units.literal: From then the countryside was untilled; all dependent prefectures became his.

units.zh: 瑄乃遣人求救於太原，李克用遣其將李承嗣、史儼等援之。
units.en: Xuan appealed to Taiyuan; Li Keyong sent Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and other generals to help.
units.literal: Xuan then sent men to beg rescue from Taiyuan; Li Keyong dispatched his generals Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and others to aid him.

units.zh: 尋為羅宏信所扼，援路既絕，瑄、瑾竟敗。
units.en: Luo Hongxin soon blocked the road; aid failed, and Xuan and Jin were ruined.
units.literal: Soon they were choked off by Luo Hongxin; the relief route cut, Xuan and Jin were defeated at last.

units.zh: 乾寧四年正月，龐師古攻陷鄆州，遁至中都北，匿於民家，為其所箠，並妻榮氏擒之來獻，俱斬於汴橋下。
units.en: In Qianning 4, month 1, Pang Shigu captured Yan. Xuan fled north of Zhongdu and hid in a peasant home; the family thrashed and seized him and Lady Rong, and both were executed at Bian Bridge.
units.literal: In the first month of Qianning year 4, Pang Shigu took Yanzhou; fleeing north of Zhongdu, hiding in a commoner's house, he was beaten by the household, and together with his wife Lady Rong was seized and presented; both were beheaded below Bian Bridge.

units.zh: 朱瑾，瑄從父弟。
units.en: Zhu Jin was Xuan's cousin.
units.literal: Zhu Jin was Xuan's younger cousin.

units.zh: 雄武絕倫，性頗殘忍。
units.en: He was peerless in battle and notoriously harsh.
units.literal: His martial valor was unmatched; his nature rather cruel.

units.zh: 光啟中，瑾與兗州節度使齊克讓婚，瑾自鄆盛飾車服，私藏兵甲，以赴禮會。
units.en: During Guangqi, Jin formed a marriage alliance with Yanzhou military commissioner Qi Kerang; he left Yun in lavish wedding gear with hidden weapons for the ceremony.
units.literal: In Guangqi, Jin formed a marriage alliance with Yanzhou military commissioner Qi Kerang; Jin came from Yun in splendid carriage and dress, secretly bearing arms and armor, to attend the wedding.

units.zh: 親迎之夜，甲士竊發，擄克讓，自稱留後。
units.en: On the wedding night his soldiers rose, kidnapped Kerang, and Jin proclaimed himself acting commissioner.
units.literal: On the night of fetching the bride, armored men sprang up secretly, seized Kerang, and Jin declared himself acting commissioner.

units.zh: 及蔡賊鴟張，瑾與太祖連衡，同討宗權，前後屢捷，以功正授兗州節度使。
units.en: As Cai rebels spread, Jin joined the Founder against Zongquan, won battle after battle, and received formal appointment as Yanzhou commissioner.
units.literal: When the Cai rebels ran wild, Jin allied with the Founder to attack Zongquan together; repeatedly victorious, for merit he was formally appointed Yanzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 既得士心，有兼並天下之意，太祖亦忌之。
units.en: He won the army's loyalty and dreamed of empire; the Founder feared him in turn.
units.literal: Once he had won the soldiers' hearts, he harbored intent to swallow the realm; the Founder also feared him.

units.zh: 瑾以厚利招誘太祖軍士，以為間諜。
units.en: Jin bribed the Founder's men into spying for him.
units.literal: Jin used rich rewards to entice the Founder's soldiers as spies.

units.zh: 及太祖攻鄆，瑾出師來援，累與太祖接戰。
units.en: Each time the Founder struck Yan, Jin came to its defense and fought him repeatedly.
units.literal: When the Founder attacked Yan, Jin marched out to aid it and clashed with the Founder again and again.

units.zh: 乾寧二年春，太祖令大將朱友恭攻瑾，掘塹柵以環之。
units.en: Spring of Qianning 2, the Founder sent Zhu Yougong against Jin with trenches and stockades encircling the city.
units.literal: In spring of Qianning year 2, the Founder ordered the great general Zhu Yougong to attack Jin, digging trenches and palisades to ring the city.

units.zh: 朱瑄遣將賀瑰及蕃將何懷寶赴援，為友恭所擒。
units.en: Xuan sent He Gui and the tribal general He Huaibao to relieve the siege; Yougong took them prisoner.
units.literal: Zhu Xuan sent the generals He Gui and the foreign officer He Huaibao to the rescue; Yougong captured them.

units.zh: 十一月，瑾從兄齊州刺史瓊以州降。
units.en: In month 11 Jin's elder cousin Qiong, prefect of Qi, surrendered his prefecture.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, Jin's elder cousin Qiong, prefect of Qi, surrendered the prefecture.

units.zh: 太祖令執賀瑰、懷寶及瓊以徇於城下，語曰：「卿兄已敗，早宜效順。」
units.en: The Founder displayed He Gui, Huaibao, and Qiong before the walls: "Your brother is beaten—yield now."
units.literal: The Founder had He Gui, Huaibao, and Qiong paraded below the wall, saying: "Your elder brother is already defeated; you should submit early."

units.zh: 瑾偽遣牙將瑚兒持書幣送降，太祖自至延壽門外，與瑾交語。
units.en: Jin feigned surrender through Hu'er with gifts; the Founder met him at the Yanshou Gate.
units.literal: Jin falsely sent the gate officer Hu'er with letter and gifts to surrender; the Founder himself came to the Yanshou Gate outside the wall to speak with Jin.

units.zh: 瑾謂太祖曰：「欲令大將送符印，願得兄瓊來押領，所貴骨肉，盡布腹心也。」
units.en: Jin told the Founder, "I will send a general with the seals; let my brother Qiong take them so kin may trust kin."
units.literal: Jin told the Founder: "I wish to have a great general deliver the tally and seal; I beg my brother Qiong come to receive them, so that flesh and blood may lay open their hearts."

units.zh: 太祖遣瓊與客將劉捍取符笥，瑾單馬立於橋上，揮手謂捍曰：「可令兄來，余有密款。」
units.en: The Founder sent Qiong with Liu Han for the tally case. Jin waited alone on the bridge and called, "Send my brother—I have a secret to share."
units.literal: The Founder sent Qiong with the guest officer Liu Han to fetch the tally box; Jin stood alone on horseback on the bridge, waved to Han and said: "Let my brother come—I have a private pledge."

units.zh: 即令瓊往。
units.en: He had Qiong come forward.
units.literal: He then ordered Qiong to advance.

units.zh: 瑾先令騎士董懷進伏於橋下，及瓊至，懷進突出，擒瓊而入，俄而斬瓊首投於城外，太祖乃班師。
units.en: Dong Huaijin lay in ambush beneath the bridge, seized Qiong, dragged him in, and beheaded him; the head was thrown outside and the Founder marched away.
units.literal: Jin had first hidden the rider Dong Huaijin under the bridge; when Qiong arrived, Huaijin burst out, seized Qiong and dragged him inside, and soon beheaded Qiong and threw the head outside the wall; the Founder then withdrew his army.

units.zh: 及鄆州陷，龐師古乘勝攻兗，瑾與李承嗣方出兵求芻粟於豐沛間，瑾之二子及大將康懷英、判官辛綰、小校閻寶以城降師古。
units.en: Yunzhou fell, and Shigu stormed Yanzhou while Jin and Li Chengsi foraged in Feng and Pei; Jin's sons, Kang Huaiying, Xin Guan, and Yan Bao handed the city to Shigu.
units.literal: When Yunzhou fell, Pang Shigu pressed his advantage and attacked Yanzhou; Jin and Li Chengsi were out foraging between Feng and Pei; Jin's two sons, the great general Kang Huaiying, the aide Xin Guan, and the petty officer Yan Bao surrendered the city to Shigu.

units.zh: 瑾無歸路，即與承嗣將麾下士將保沂州，刺史尹處賓拒關不納，乃保海州。
units.en: Cut off, Jin and Chengsi aimed for Yizhou; Yin Chubin closed the gates, so they clung to Haizhou.
units.literal: Jin had no road home; he and Chengsi led their followers intending to hold Yizhou, but prefect Yin Chubin shut the passes and would not admit them, so they held Haizhou.

units.zh: 為師古所迫，遂擁州民渡淮依楊行密。
units.en: Shigu drove them on until they fled across the Huai with their people to Yang Xingmi.
units.literal: Pressed by Shigu, they then drove the prefecture's people across the Huai to rely on Yang Xingmi.

units.zh: 行密表瑾領徐州節度使。
units.en: Xingmi had Jin appointed military commissioner of Xuzhou.
units.literal: Xingmi memorialized that Jin should hold the post of Xuzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 龐師古渡淮，行密令瑾率師以禦之，清口之敗，瑾有力焉。
units.en: Shigu crossed the Huai; Xingmi sent Jin to meet him, and Jin was decisive at Qingkou.
units.literal: When Pang Shigu crossed the Huai, Xingmi ordered Jin to lead troops against him; at the defeat of Qingkou, Jin contributed greatly.

units.zh: 自是瑾率淮軍連歲北寇徐、宿，大為東南之患。
units.en: Thereafter Jin's Huai armies raided Xu and Su yearly and plagued the southeast.
units.literal: From then Jin led Huai troops year after year raiding north into Xu and Su, a great scourge to the southeast.

units.zh: 及行密卒，子渭繼立，以徐溫子知訓為行軍副使，寵遇頗深。
units.en: After Xingmi's death his son Wei ruled and favored Xu Wen's son Zhixun as deputy commander of the field army.
units.literal: When Xingmi died, his son Wei succeeded; he made Xu Wen's son Zhixun deputy commander of the campaign army, with deep favor.

units.zh: 後楊溥僭號，知訓為樞密使，知政事，以瑾為同平章事，仍督親軍。
units.en: When Yang Pu claimed kingship, Zhixun ran military affairs and government; Jin became co-equal chief minister and kept command of the guard.
units.literal: Later when Yang Pu usurped the title, Zhixun became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and handled government affairs; Jin was made co-equal chief minister and still directed the personal guard.

units.zh: 時徐溫父子恃寵專政，慮瑾不附己。
units.en: The Xu clan, arrogant in power, feared Jin would not obey them.
units.literal: At that time the Xu father and son, relying on favor, monopolized government, fearing Jin would not side with them.

units.zh: 〈（陳彭年《江南別錄》云：徐知訓初學兵法於朱瑾，瑾悉心教之。
units.en: (Chen Pengnian's 《Separate Record of Jiangnan》 records that Zhixun first learned warfare from Jin, who taught him earnestly.
units.literal: (Chen Pengnian's 《Separate Record of Jiangnan》 says: Xu Zhixun at first studied military arts under Zhu Jin; Jin taught him with all his heart.

units.zh: 後與瑾有隙，夜遣壯士殺瑾，瑾手刃數人，埋於舍後。）〉
units.en: Later they quarreled; Zhixun sent killers by night and Jin slew several before he was buried behind his house.)〉
units.literal: Later he had a rift with Jin and by night sent braves to kill Jin; Jin cut down several men with his own hand and was buried behind his quarters.)〉

units.zh: 貞明四年六月，出瑾為淮寧軍節度使。
units.en: In Zhenming 4, month 6, Jin was posted out as commissioner of Huaining.
units.literal: In the sixth month of Zhenming year 4, Jin was transferred out to be military commissioner of Huaining.

units.zh: 知訓設家宴以餞瑾，瑾事之逾遜。
units.en: Zhixun held a farewell feast at home; Jin was more obsequious than ever.
units.literal: Zhixun gave a family feast to send Jin off; Jin served him with even greater deference.

units.zh: 翌日，詣知訓第謝，留門久之，知訓家僮私謂瑾曰：「政事相公此夕在白牡丹妓院，侍者無得往。」
units.en: Next day he called to thank Zhixun and lingered at the gate; a servant whispered, "The chief minister is at the White Peony brothel tonight—no attendants allowed."
units.literal: The next day he called at Zhixun's residence to thank him and waited long at the gate; Zhixun's household slaves privately told Jin: "The chief minister of government tonight is at the White Peony courtesan's house—attendants must not go."

units.zh: 瑾謂典謁曰：「吾不奈朝饑，且歸。」
units.en: Jin told the usher, "I cannot bear the morning hunger; I am going home."
units.literal: Jin told the usher: "I cannot bear the morning hunger; I will return."

units.zh: 既而知訓聞之，愕然曰：「晚當過瑾。」
units.en: Zhixun, startled, said, "I should visit Jin this evening."
units.literal: When Zhixun heard it he said in alarm: "I should visit Jin this evening."

units.zh: 瑾厚備供帳。
units.en: Jin laid out a rich feast and lodging.
units.literal: Jin lavishly prepared provisions and lodging.

units.zh: 瑾有所乘名馬，冬以錦帳貯之，夏以羅幬護之。
units.en: His prized horse slept under brocade in winter and gauze awnings in summer.
units.literal: Jin had a famous horse; in winter it was stored in brocade curtains, in summer protected by gauze canopies.

units.zh: 愛妓桃氏，有絕色，善歌舞。
units.en: His favorite Tao was a peerless singer and dancer.
units.literal: His beloved concubine Lady Tao had supreme beauty and was skilled in song and dance.

units.zh: 及知訓至，奉卮酒為壽，初以名馬奉，知訓喜而言曰：「相公出鎮，與吾暫別，離恨可知，願此盡歡。」
units.en: Zhixun came; Jin toasted him and gave the horse. Zhixun said, "You leave office and leave me—our parting hurts; let us drink deep."
units.literal: When Zhixun arrived, Jin offered a cup of wine for long life; first he presented the famous horse; Zhixun said with pleasure: "The chief minister leaves his post for a time apart from me—parting sorrow is plain; let us drink our fill."

units.zh: 瑾即延知訓於中堂，出桃氏，酒既醉，瑾斬知訓首，示其部下。
units.en: In the main hall he brought out Tao; when Zhixun was drunk Jin struck off his head and displayed it to the army.
units.literal: Jin then led Zhixun into the central hall, brought out Lady Tao, and when wine had muddled him, Jin cut off Zhixun's head and showed it to his troops.

units.zh: 因以其眾急趨衙城，知訓之黨已闔門矣，唯瑾得獨入，與衙兵戰。
units.en: He raced for the government compound; Zhixun's men had barred the gates—only Jin broke in and fought the guard.
units.literal: Then with his men he rushed to the yamen city; Zhixun's faction had already shut the gates; only Jin entered alone and fought the yamen soldiers.

units.zh: 復逾城而出，傷足，求馬不獲，遂自刎。
units.en: He scaled the wall wounded, found no horse, and killed himself.
units.literal: He climbed the wall again to get out, wounded in the foot, sought a horse and could not find one, and cut his own throat.

units.zh: 暴其屍於市，盛夏無蠅蛆，徐溫令投之於江，部人竊收葬之。
units.en: His body lay in the market untouched by flies; Wen had it cast into the river, but townsfolk secretly buried it.
units.literal: His corpse was exposed in the market; in midsummer no flies or maggots came; Xu Wen ordered it thrown into the river, but the people secretly recovered and buried it.

units.zh: 溫疾亟，夢瑾被髮引滿將射之。
units.en: Wen, deathly ill, dreamed Jin with loose hair drawing a bow at him.
units.literal: When Wen fell gravely ill, he dreamed Jin, hair loose, drawing a full bow to shoot him.

units.zh: 溫乃為之禮葬，立祠以祭之。
units.en: Wen buried him with rites and raised a shrine.
units.literal: Wen then gave him a ceremonial burial and built a shrine to sacrifice to him.

units.zh: 〈（馬令《南唐書》云：初，宿衛將李球、馬謙挾楊隆演登樓，取庫兵以誅知訓，陣於門橋。
units.en: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》 says guards Li Qiu and Ma Qian seized Longyan, armed from the storehouse to kill Zhixun, and formed ranks at the gate bridge.
units.literal: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》 says: At first the palace guards Li Qiu and Ma Qian seized Yang Longyan, climbed the tower, took arsenal weapons to execute Zhixun, and formed battle lines at the gate bridge.

units.zh: 知訓與戰，頻卻。
units.en: Zhixun fought and was driven back again and again.
units.literal: Zhixun fought them and was repeatedly driven back.

units.zh: 朱瑾適自外來，以一騎前視其陣，曰：「不足為也。」
units.en: Jin rode in from outside, scanned the line, and said, "This is nothing."
units.literal: Zhu Jin happened to come from outside, rode forward alone to view their formation, and said: "They are not worth dealing with."

units.zh: 因反顧一麾，外兵爭進，遂斬球、謙，亂兵皆潰。
units.en: He wheeled and signaled; outside troops poured in, killed Qiu and Qian, and the mob scattered.
units.literal: Then he turned and waved once; the outer troops rushed in together, beheaded Qiu and Qian, and the disorderly soldiers all fled.

units.zh: 瑾嘗有德於知訓者也，及其凶終，吳人皆謂曲在知訓。
units.en: Jin had once aided Zhixun; when he died violently, Wu opinion blamed Zhixun.
units.literal: Jin had once shown kindness to Zhixun; at his violent end, the Wu people all said the fault lay with Zhixun.

units.zh: 《五代史補》：瑾之奔淮南也，時行密方圖霸，其為禮待，有加於諸將數等。
units.en: The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 notes that when Jin reached Huainan, Xingmi, planning supremacy, honored him above other commanders.
units.literal: 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: When Jin fled to Huainan, Xingmi was then planning hegemony and treated him with courtesy beyond other generals.

units.zh: 瑾感行密見知，欲立奇功為報，但憾無入陣馬，忽忽不樂。
units.en: Grateful for Xingmi's trust, he longed to repay with a brilliant victory but lacked a battle horse and brooded.
units.literal: Jin, moved by Xingmi's recognition, wished to repay with a striking deed, but regretted having no charger for the charge; he was restless and unhappy.

units.zh: 一日晝寢，夢老叟，眉發皓然，謂謹曰：「君長憾無入陣馬，今馬生矣！」
units.en: At noon he dreamed a white-haired elder saying, "You lamented no war horse—now one is born!"
units.literal: One day at noon he napped and dreamed an old man, eyebrows and hair snow-white, who said to Jin: "You long regretted having no charger for the charge—now a horse is born!"

units.zh: 及廄隸報，適退槽馬生一駒，見臥未能起。
units.en: The groom reported a foal just dropped in the stable, still unable to stand.
units.literal: When the stable boy reported that a foal had just been born in the manger, he saw it lying unable to rise.

units.zh: 瑾驚曰：「何應之速也！」
units.en: Jin exclaimed in alarm, "How fast the omen came!"
units.literal: Jin said in alarm: "How swiftly it answered!"

units.zh: 行往視之，見骨目皆非常馬，大喜曰：「事辦矣！」
units.en: Jin inspected it—bone and eye unlike any common horse—and cried in delight, "The affair is done!"
units.literal: Jin went to look; its bone and eyes were all unlike an ordinary horse; greatly pleased he said: "The affair is done!"

units.zh: 其後破杜洪，取鍾傳，未嘗不得力焉。
units.en: Later, against Du Hong and Zhong Chuan, that horse never failed him.
units.literal: Afterward in breaking Du Hong and taking Zhong Chuan he never failed to rely on its strength.

units.zh: 初，瑾之來也，徐溫睹其英烈，深忌之，故瑾不敢預政。
units.en: When Jin arrived, Xu Wen feared his brilliance and kept him from politics.
units.literal: At first, when Jin came, Xu Wen saw his heroism and deeply feared him, so Jin did not dare enter government.

units.zh: 及行密死，子溥嗣位，溫與張鎬爭權，襲殺鎬，自是事無大小，皆決於溫。
units.en: After Xingmi's death Pu ruled; Wen killed rival Zhang Hao and thereafter decided everything.
units.literal: When Xingmi died and his son Pu succeeded, Wen and Zhang Hao struggled for power; Wen ambushed and killed Hao, and from then matters great and small were all decided by Wen.

units.zh: 既而溫復為自安之計，乃以子知訓自代，然後引兵出居金陵，實欲控製中外。
units.en: Wen then installed Zhixun in his place and moved to Jinling with an army to rule court and provinces alike.
units.literal: Then Wen, for his own security, placed his son Zhixun in his stead, and only then led troops out to dwell at Jinling, in truth intending to control inside and outside.

units.zh: 知訓尤恣橫，瑾居常嫉之。
units.en: Zhixun grew tyrannical; Jin hated him.
units.literal: Zhixun was especially overbearing; Jin constantly resented him.

units.zh: 一旦知訓欲得瑾所乘馬，瑾怒，遂擊殺知訓，提其首請溥起兵誅溫。
units.en: When Zhixun demanded his horse, Jin killed him, seized his head, and urged Pu to mobilize against Wen.
units.literal: One day when Zhixun wanted Jin's horse, Jin in anger struck and killed Zhixun, raised his head and begged Pu to raise troops to execute Wen.

units.zh: 溥素怯懦，見之掩麵而走。
units.en: Timid Pu covered his face and fled.
units.literal: Pu was by nature timid; seeing it he covered his face and ran.

units.zh: 瑾曰：「老婢兒不足為計！」
units.en: Jin said, "That son of an old slave-woman is not worth planning for!"
units.literal: Jin said: "The son of an old slave-woman is not worth planning for!"

units.zh: 亦自殺，中外大駭且懼。
units.en: He too took his own life, and court and country panicked.
units.literal: He too killed himself; inside and outside were greatly alarmed and afraid.

units.zh: 溫至，遽以瑾屍暴之市中。
units.en: Wen came and at once displayed Jin's body in the market.
units.literal: When Wen arrived, he immediately exposed Jin's corpse in the market.

units.zh: 時盛暑，肌肉累日不壞，至青蠅無敢輒泊。
units.en: In midsummer the corpse did not rot for days; flies would not touch it.
units.literal: It was high summer; the flesh for many days did not decay; even green flies did not dare alight.

units.zh: 人有病者，或於暴屍處取土煎而服之，無不愈。）〉
units.en: The sick took soil from the exposed corpse, brewed it as medicine, and were invariably cured.)〉
units.literal: When people fell ill, some took earth from where the corpse was exposed, boiled it, and drank it—all were cured without exception.)〉

units.zh: 時溥，徐州人，初為州之驍將。
units.en: Shi Pu of Xuzhou began as one of the province's fiercest officers.
units.literal: Shi Pu was a man of Xuzhou; at first he was a fierce general of the prefecture.

units.zh: 唐中和初，秦宗權據蔡州，侵寇鄰藩，節度使支詳命溥率師以討之，徐軍屢捷，軍情歸順，以節鉞授之。
units.en: Early in Zhonghe, Zongquan held Caizhou and harried the borders; Zhi Xiang sent Pu against him; Xu troops won again and again until the army chose Pu and gave him the commission.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tang Zhonghe, Qin Zongquan held Caizhou and raided neighboring circuits; military commissioner Zhi Xiang ordered Pu to lead troops against him; Xu armies won repeatedly, the army's hearts turned to him, and the command seal was given him.

units.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》列傳云：時溥，彭城人，徐之牙將。
units.en: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 calls Pu a Pengcheng man and a Xu staff officer.
units.literal: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 biography says: Shi Pu, a man of Pengcheng, was a junior officer of Xu.

units.zh: 黃巢據長安，詔征天下兵進討。
units.en: When Huang Chao seized Chang'an, the throne called the empire to arms.
units.literal: When Huang Chao held Chang'an, an edict summoned troops from all the realm to advance and attack.

units.zh: 中和二年，武寧軍節度使支詳遣溥與副將陳璠率師五千赴難，行至河陰，軍亂，剽河陰縣回。
units.en: Zhonghe year 2, Zhi Xiang sent Pu and Chen Fan with five thousand men toward the capital; at Heyin the troops mutinied and looted the county on the march back.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe, Wuning military commissioner Zhi Xiang sent Pu with deputy general Chen Fan to lead five thousand men to the rescue; reaching Heyin, the army mutinied and plundered Heyin county on the return.

units.zh: 溥招合撫諭，其眾復集，懼罪，屯於境上。
units.en: Pu rallied them, but fearing punishment they halted on the frontier.
units.literal: Pu gathered and comforted them; the masses reassembled; fearing guilt, they camped on the border.

units.zh: 詳遣人迎犒，悉恕之，溥乃移軍向徐州。
units.en: Xiang sent envoys with gifts and a full pardon; Pu then marched on Xuzhou.
units.literal: Xiang sent men to welcome them with rewards and fully pardoned them; Pu then shifted the army toward Xuzhou.

units.zh: 既入，軍人大呼，推溥為留後。
units.en: Entering the city, the troops roared and made Pu acting commissioner.
units.literal: Once inside, the soldiers shouted greatly and pushed Pu to be acting commissioner.

units.zh: 送詳於大彭館。
units.en: They lodged Xiang at the Great Peng guesthouse.
units.literal: They sent Xiang to the Great Peng lodge.

units.zh: 溥大出資裝，遣陳璠援詳歸京。
units.en: Pu paid lavishly from his treasury and sent Chen Fan to escort Xiang to court.
units.literal: Pu spent heavily from his stores and sent Chen Fan to escort Xiang back to the capital.

units.zh: 詳宿七里亭，其夜為璠所殺，舉家屠害。
units.en: Xiang stopped at Qili Pavilion; that night Fan murdered him and butchered his household.
units.literal: Xiang lodged at Qili Pavilion; that night Fan killed him, and the whole family was slaughtered.

units.zh: 溥以璠為宿州刺史，竟以違命殺詳，溥誅璠，又令別將帥軍三千赴難京師。
units.en: Pu made Chen Fan prefect of Su, then executed him for killing Xiang; another general led three thousand men to aid the capital.
units.literal: Pu made Chen Fan prefect of Su; because Chen Fan had killed Xiang against orders, Pu executed him and ordered another general to lead three thousand men to the capital for the rescue.

units.zh: 天子還宮，授之節鉞。
units.en: When the emperor returned to the palace, Pu received the commission.
units.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace, he granted Pu the command seal.

units.zh: 及黃巢攻陳州，秦宗權據蔡州，與賊連結，徐、蔡相近，溥出師討之，軍鋒益盛，每戰屢捷。
units.en: Chao besieged Chenzhou while Zongquan held Caizhou; Pu struck from nearby Xu and won battle after battle.
units.literal: When Huang Chao attacked Chenzhou, Qin Zongquan held Caizhou and linked with the bandits; Xu and Cai were near; Pu marched out to attack and his army's edge grew keener; in every battle he won repeatedly.

units.zh: 黃巢之敗也，其將尚讓以數千人降溥。
units.en: After Chao's fall, his general Shang Rang surrendered several thousand men to Pu.
units.literal: When Huang Chao was defeated, his general Shang Rang surrendered to Pu with several thousand men.

units.zh: 後林言又斬黃巢首歸徐州。
units.en: Later Lin Yan delivered Chao's head to Xuzhou.
units.literal: Later Lin Yan also sent Huang Chao's head to Xuzhou.

units.zh: 時溥功居第一，詔授檢校太尉、中書令、钜鹿郡王。
units.en: Pu's merit ranked first; the court made him honorary Grand Marshal, Grand Secretary, and Prince of Julu.
units.literal: At that time Pu's merit ranked first; an edict appointed him honorary Grand Marshal, Grand Secretary, and Prince of Julu.

units.zh: 宗權未平，仍授溥徐州行營兵馬都統。
units.en: While Zongquan still stood, Pu was named commander of Xu's field armies.
units.literal: Zongquan not yet pacified, Pu was still appointed overall commander of Xu's campaign army and horse.

units.zh: 蔡賊平，朱全忠與之爭功，遂相嫌怨。
units.en: After Cai fell, Zhu Quanzhong quarreled over credit and hatred grew.
units.literal: When the Cai rebels were pacified, Zhu Quanzhong disputed merit with him, and mutual resentment arose.

units.zh: 淮南亂，朝廷以全忠遙領淮南節度，以平孫儒、行密之亂。
units.en: Huainan rebelled; the court named Quanzhong distant commissioner to crush Sun Ru and Yang Xingmi.
units.literal: When Huainan fell into disorder, the court had Quanzhong hold Huainan military commission at a distance to pacify Sun Ru and Yang Xingmi's turmoil.

units.zh: 汴人應援，路出徐方，溥阻之。
units.en: Bian troops marched through Xu; Pu barred the road.
units.literal: Bian men came to aid; the road passed through Xu territory; Pu blocked them.

units.zh: 全忠怒，出師攻徐。
units.en: Quanzhong attacked Xu in fury.
units.literal: Quanzhong was angry and sent troops to attack Xu.

units.zh: 自光啟至大順，六七年間，汴軍四集，徐、泗三郡，民無耕稼，頻歲水災，人喪十六七。
units.en: For six or seven years Bian armies swarmed; Xu and Si lay untilled through flood and war until six or seven in ten were dead.
units.literal: From Guangqi to Datong, six or seven years, Bian armies gathered four times; in Xu, Si, and the three prefectures the people did not plow; years of flood followed; men lost six or seven in ten.

units.zh: 溥窘蹙，求和於汴，全忠曰：「移鎮則可。」
units.en: Desperate, Pu sued for peace; Quanzhong said, "Move your post and we may talk."
units.literal: Pu in straits sought peace with Bian; Quanzhong said: "Transfer your commission and it can be done."

units.zh: 朝廷以尚書劉崇望代溥，以溥為太子太師。
units.en: The court sent Liu Chongwang to replace Pu and made Pu Grand Preceptor of the Heir.
units.literal: The court made Minister Liu Chongwang replace Pu, and made Pu Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 溥懼出城見害，不受代。
units.en: Fearing murder if he left the walls, Pu refused to yield.
units.literal: Pu feared leaving the city and being harmed, and did not accept replacement.

units.zh: 汴將龐師古陳兵於野，溥求援於兗州，朱瑾出兵救之；
units.en: Pang Shigu camped in the open; Pu begged Yanzhou; Zhu Jin marched to his aid;
units.literal: Bian general Pang Shigu arrayed troops in the field; Pu sought aid from Yanzhou; Zhu Jin marched to rescue him;

units.zh: 值大雪，糧盡而還。
units.en: Snow blocked them; supplies failed and Jin turned back.
units.literal: Heavy snow fell; grain ran out and they returned.

units.zh: 城中守陴者饑甚，加之疾疫，汴將王重師、牛存節夜乘梯而入，溥與妻子登樓自焚而卒，實景福二年也。
units.en: Defenders starved and sickened; Wang Chongshi and Niu Cunjie scaled the walls by night; Pu and his family burned themselves on a tower in Jingfu year 2.
units.literal: Those defending the walls were desperately hungry; plague added to it; Bian generals Wang Chongshi and Niu Cunjie entered by night on ladders; Pu and his wife and children ascended a tower and burned themselves to death—it was in fact Jingfu year 2.

units.zh: 地入於汴。）〉
units.en: Xu fell to Bian.)〉
units.literal: The land passed to Bian.)〉

units.zh: 王師範，青州人。
units.en: Wang Shifan came from Qingzhou.
units.literal: Wang Shifan was a man of Qingzhou.

units.zh: 父敬武，初為平盧牙將。
units.en: His father Jingwu began as a Pinglu staff officer.
units.literal: His father Jingwu at first was a Pinglu junior officer.

units.zh: 唐廣明元年，無棣人洪霸郎合群盜於齊、棣間，節度使安師儒遣敬武討平之。
units.en: Guangming year 1, Hong Balang raided Qi and Di; An Shiru sent Jingwu to crush him.
units.literal: In the first year of Tang Guangming, the Wudi man Hong Balang gathered bandits between Qi and Di; military commissioner An Shiru sent Jingwu to pacify them.

units.zh: 及巢賊犯長安，諸藩擅易主帥，敬武乃逐師儒，自為留後。
units.en: As Chao ravaged Chang'an, circuits changed commanders at will; Jingwu expelled Shiru and seized the post.
units.literal: When the Chao bandits invaded Chang'an, the various circuits arbitrarily changed their commanders; Jingwu then drove out Shiru and made himself acting commissioner.

units.zh: 王鐸承製授以節鉞，後以出師勤王功，加太尉、平章事。
units.en: Wang Duo invested him by imperial order; later aid to the throne won him Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.
units.literal: Wang Duo by imperial order granted the command seal; later for merit in marching to aid the Son of Heaven he was raised to Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.

units.zh: 龍紀中，敬武卒，師範年幼，三軍推之為帥，棣州刺史張蟾叛於師範，不受節度，朝廷乃以崔安潛為平盧帥，師範拒命。
units.en: In Longji Jingwu died; the army made young Shifan commander; Di prefect Zhang Chan rebelled; the court named Cui Anqian commander and Shifan defied him.
units.literal: In Longji, Jingwu died; Shifan was young; the three armies pushed him as commander; Di prefect Zhang Chan rebelled against Shifan and would not accept his command; the court then made Cui Anqian Pinglu commander, and Shifan refused the order.

units.zh: 張蟾迎安潛至郡，同討師範。
units.en: Chan welcomed Anqian and jointly attacked Shifan.
units.literal: Zhang Chan welcomed Anqian to the prefecture and together attacked Shifan.

units.zh: 師範遣將盧宏將兵攻蟾，宏復叛，與蟾通謀，偽旋軍將襲青州。
units.en: Shifan sent Lu Hong against Chan; Hong turned traitor, plotted with Chan, and feigned retreat to strike Qingzhou.
units.literal: Shifan sent the general Lu Hong with troops to attack Chan; Hong rebelled again, conspired with Chan, and feigned a withdrawal to strike Qingzhou.

units.zh: 師範知之，遣重賂迎宏，謂之曰：「吾以先人之故，為軍府所推，年方幼少，未能幹事。
units.en: Shifan learned of it, welcomed Hong with gifts, and said, "The army made me commander because of my father; I am young and cannot rule.
units.literal: Shifan knew it; sent rich gifts to welcome Hong, and told him: "Because of my father's matter I am pushed by the military government; I am still young and cannot manage affairs.

units.zh: 如公以先人之故，令不乏祀，公之仁也。
units.en: If you preserve our ancestral rites for my father's sake, that is mercy.
units.literal: If you, sir, because of my father's matter keep our sacrifices from failing, that is your benevolence.

units.zh: 如以為難與成事，乞保首領，以守先人墳墓，亦惟命。」
units.en: If you think me unfit, let me keep my head and tend the tombs—that is all I ask."
units.literal: If you find it hard to succeed with me, I beg to keep my head and guard my ancestors' graves—that too is as you command."

units.zh: 宏以師範年幼，必無能為，不為之備。
units.en: Hong thought the boy helpless and took no precautions.
units.literal: Hong, because Shifan was young, was certain he could do nothing and made no preparations.

units.zh: 師範伏兵要路，迎而享之，預謂紀綱劉鄩曰：「翌日盧宏至，爾即斬之，酬爾以軍校。」
units.en: Shifan ambushed the road, feasted Hong, and told Liu Ye, "When Hong comes tomorrow, strike off his head and I will make you a field officer."
units.literal: Shifan set ambush on the road, welcomed and feasted him, and beforehand told the steward Liu Ye: "Tomorrow when Lu Hong arrives, you cut off his head; I will reward you with a field officer's post."

units.zh: 鄩如其言，斬宏於座上，及同亂者數人。
units.en: Ye beheaded Hong at the feast and several conspirators with him.
units.literal: Ye did as told and beheaded Hong at table, and several co-rebels as well.

units.zh: 因戒厲士眾，大行頒賞，與之誓約，自率之以攻棣州，擒張蟾，斬之。
units.en: He rallied the army with rewards and oaths, led them against Di, captured Zhang Chan, and executed him.
units.literal: Then he sternly warned the troops, gave great rewards, made oaths with them, personally led them to attack Di prefecture, seized Zhang Chan, and beheaded him.

units.zh: 安潛遁還長安。
units.en: Anqian fled to Chang'an.
units.literal: Anqian fled back to Chang'an.

units.zh: 師範雅好儒術，少負縱橫之學，故安民禁暴，各有方略，當時藩翰咸稱之。
units.en: He loved scholarship and stratagem, ruled with measured force, and frontier lords praised him.
units.literal: Shifan elegantly loved Confucian learning, in youth bore horizontal-and-vertical arts, so in calming the people and forbidding violence he had measures each in place; the frontier governors of the time all praised him.

units.zh: 及太祖平兗、鄆，遣朱友恭攻之，師範乞盟，遂與通好。
units.en: After the Founder took Yan, Yougong attacked; Shifan sued for peace and they allied.
units.literal: When the Founder pacified Yan and Yanzhou, he sent Zhu Yougong to attack him; Shifan begged alliance and then was on friendly terms.

units.zh: 天復元年冬，李茂貞劫遷車駕幸鳳翔，韓全誨矯詔加罪於太祖，令方鎮出師赴難。
units.en: Tianfu 1 winter, Maozhen seized the emperor at Fengxiang; Quanhui forged an edict condemning the Founder and summoned the circuits.
units.literal: In winter of Tianfu year 1, Li Maozhen seized and moved the imperial carriage to Fengxiang; Han Quanhui forged an edict adding crimes to the Founder and ordered the circuits to march troops to the rescue.

units.zh: 詔至青州，師範承詔泣下曰：「吾輩為天子藩籬，君父有難，略無奮力者，皆強兵自衛，縱賊如此，使上失守宗祧，危而不持，是誰之過，吾今日成敗以之！」
units.en: The edict reached Qingzhou; Shifan wept and said, "We are the emperor's shield, yet none fights while the throne is lost—whose fault? Today I stake everything on this!"
units.literal: When the edict reached Qingzhou, Shifan received it with tears and said: "We are the Son of Heaven's screen; the lord and father is in difficulty, yet none strives with force—all keep strong armies for themselves and let bandits go so far that the sovereign loses the altars of state; peril without support—whose fault is it? Today I stake success or failure on this!"

units.zh: 乃發使通楊行密，遣將劉鄩襲兗州，別將襲齊。
units.en: He contacted Yang Xingmi, sent Liu Ye against Yanzhou, and struck Qi.
units.literal: He then sent envoys to Yang Xingmi and dispatched Liu Ye to raid Yanzhou while another column struck Qi.

units.zh: 時太祖方圍鳳翔，師範遣將張居厚部輿夫二百，言有獻於太祖。
units.en: While the Founder besieged Fengxiang, Shifan sent Zhang Juhou with two hundred carts claiming tribute.
units.literal: At that time the Founder was besieging Fengxiang; Shifan sent the general Zhang Juhou with two hundred cart bearers, saying there was tribute for the Founder.

units.zh: 至華州城東，華將婁敬思疑其有異，剖輿視之，乃兵仗也。
units.en: East of Huazhou, Lou Jingsi opened the carts and found weapons.
units.literal: Reaching east of Huazhou city, Hua general Lou Jingsi suspected something amiss, opened the carts and looked—inside were weapons.

units.zh: 居厚等因呼，殺敬思，聚眾攻西城。
units.en: They killed Jingsi, rallied men, and stormed the west gate.
units.literal: Juhou and the rest then shouted, killed Jingsi, gathered the masses, and attacked the west gate.

units.zh: 時崔胤在華州，遣部下閉關拒之，遂遁去。
units.en: Cui Yin at Huazhou shut the gates and drove them off.
units.literal: That day Cui Yin was at Huazhou; he sent subordinates to shut the passes and repel them, and they fled.

units.zh: 是日，劉鄩下兗州，河南數十郡同日發。
units.en: That day Ye took Yanzhou; dozens of Henan prefectures rebelled together.
units.literal: That day Liu Ye took Yanzhou; several tens of prefectures in Henan rose on the same day.

units.zh: 太祖怒，遣朱友寧率軍討之。
units.en: The Founder sent Zhu Youning to punish him.
units.literal: The Founder was angry and sent Zhu Youning with troops to attack.

units.zh: 既而友寧為青軍所敗，臨陣被擒，傳首於淮南。
units.en: Youning was defeated, captured, and his head sent to Huainan.
units.literal: Soon Youning was defeated by Qing troops, captured in battle, and his head was sent to Huainan.

units.zh: 天復三年七月，太祖復令楊師厚進攻，屯於臨朐。
units.en: Tianfu 3, month 7, Yang Shihou advanced and camped at Linqu.
units.literal: In the seventh month of Tianfu year 3, the Founder again ordered Yang Shihou to advance; he camped at Linqu.

units.zh: 師厚屢敗青軍，遂進寨於城下。
units.en: Shihou beat Qing armies repeatedly and pitched camp under the walls.
units.literal: Shihou repeatedly defeated Qing troops and then advanced his camp below the city.

units.zh: 師範懼，乃令副使李嗣業詣師厚乞降，
units.en: Afraid, Shifan sent Li Siye to beg Shihou for terms,
units.literal: Shifan in fear then ordered deputy envoy Li Siye to go to Shihou and beg surrender,

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》云：師厚圍青州，敗師範兵於臨朐，執諸將，又獲其弟師克。
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says Shihou took Qingzhou, beat Shifan at Linqu, captured his generals and brother Shike.
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Shihou besieged Qingzhou, defeated Shifan's army at Linqu, captured the generals, and also took his younger brother Shike.

units.zh: 是時師範眾尚十餘萬，諸將請決戰，而師範以弟故，乃請降。）〉
units.en: Shifan still had a hundred thousand men; his officers wanted battle, but for his brother's sake he surrendered.)〉
units.literal: At that time Shifan's masses still numbered more than a hundred thousand; the generals asked for a decisive battle, but because of his brother Shifan requested surrender.)〉

units.zh: 太祖許之。
units.en: The Founder agreed.
units.literal: The Founder permitted it.

units.zh: 歲餘，遣李振權典青州事，因令師範舉家徙汴。
units.en: A year later Li Zhen governed Qingzhou while Shifan moved his family to Bian.
units.literal: After more than a year he sent Li Zhen to administer Qingzhou affairs provisionally and ordered Shifan to move his whole household to Bian.

units.zh: 師範將至，縞素乘驢，請罪於太祖。
units.en: He came in white on a donkey to beg the Founder's pardon.
units.literal: When Shifan was about to arrive, in white mourning he rode a donkey and asked forgiveness of the Founder.

units.zh: 太祖以禮待之，尋表為河陽節度使。
units.en: The Founder honored him and soon made him commissioner of Heyang.
units.literal: The Founder treated him with courtesy and soon memorialized him as military commissioner of Heyang.

units.zh: 會韓建移鎮青州，太祖帳餞於郊，師範預焉。
units.en: When Han Jian took Qingzhou, the Founder feasted him outside the city; Shifan attended.
units.literal: When Han Jian was transferred to govern Qingzhou, the Founder feasted him in the suburbs; Shifan was present.

units.zh: 太祖謂建曰：「公頃在華陰，政事之暇，省覽經籍，此亦士君子之大務。
units.en: The Founder told Jian, "At Huayin you read the classics in quiet hours—that is a gentleman's duty.
units.literal: The Founder told Jian: "You, sir, formerly at Huayin in the leisure of government affairs read the classics—this too is a great task of gentlemen.

units.zh: 今之青土，政簡務暇，可復修華陰之故事。」
units.en: Qing is quiet now; resume your Huayin studies."
units.literal: Today Qing territory has simple government and leisure; you may again practice Huayin's old ways."

units.zh: 建撝謙而已。
units.en: Jian demurred.
units.literal: Jian made modest disclaimers only.

units.zh: 太祖又曰：「公讀書必須精意，勿錯用心。」
units.en: The Founder added, "Read with care—do not misapply your mind."
units.literal: The Founder also said: "When you read you must concentrate your mind—do not use it wrongly."

units.zh: 太祖以師範好儒，前以青州叛，故以此言譏之。
units.en: He mocked Shifan's love of learning because Qing had rebelled.
units.literal: Because Shifan loved the Ruists, and earlier Qingzhou had rebelled, he spoke thus to mock him.

units.zh: 及太祖即位，征為金吾上將軍。
units.en: When the Founder became emperor, Shifan was summoned as Golden Guard general.
units.literal: When the Founder took the throne, he was summoned as General of the Golden Guard.

units.zh: 開平初，太祖封諸子為王，友寧妻號訴於太祖曰：「陛下化家為國，人人皆得封崇。
units.en: At Kaiping the Founder enfeoffed his sons; Youning's widow cried, "You ennoble everyone while my husband died because Shifan rebelled—what was his crime?
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping, the Founder enfeoffed his sons as kings; Youning's wife cried out to the Founder: "Your Majesty has turned the family into a state; every man receives enfeoffment and honor.

units.zh: 妾夫早預艱難，粗立勞效，不幸師範反逆，亡夫橫屍疆場。
units.en: He served in hardship and died on the border when Shifan turned traitor.
units.literal: My husband early shared hardship and roughly established merit; unluckily Shifan rebelled, and my husband lay dead on the frontier.

units.zh: 冤仇尚在朝廷，受陛下恩澤，亡夫何罪！」
units.en: The killer still enjoys your grace—what did my husband do wrong!"
units.literal: The enemy still lives at court, receiving Your Majesty's grace—what crime had my husband!"

units.zh: 太祖淒然泣下曰：「幾忘此賊。」
units.en: The Founder wept, "I had nearly forgotten that villain."
units.literal: The Founder said tearfully: "I nearly forgot this bandit."

units.zh: 即遣人族師範於洛陽。
units.en: He sent men to wipe out Shifan's clan at Luoyang.
units.literal: He immediately sent men to exterminate Shifan's clan at Luoyang.

units.zh: 先掘坑於第側，乃告之，其弟師誨、兄師悅及兒侄二百口，鹹盡戮焉。
units.en: A pit was dug by his house; Shihui, Shiyue, and two hundred kin were slaughtered.
units.literal: First they dug a pit beside the residence, then announced it; his younger brother Shihui, elder brother Shiyue, and sons and nephews two hundred mouths were all slaughtered.

units.zh: 時使者宣詔訖，師範盛啟宴席，令昆仲子弟列座，謂使者曰：「死者人所不能免，況有罪乎！
units.en: After the edict was read Shifan feasted his kin and told the envoy, "Death comes to all—especially the guilty.
units.literal: When the envoy had read the edict, Shifan set a full banquet and seated brothers and nephews in order, telling the envoy: "Death is what no man can escape—how much more when guilty!

units.zh: 然予懼坑屍於下，少長失序，恐有愧於先人。」
units.en: Yet I fear disorder in the pit and shame to our ancestors."
units.literal: Yet I fear being thrown into the pit below with young and old out of order—I would shame our ancestors."

units.zh: 行酒之次，令少長依次於坑所受戮，人士痛之。
units.en: He had them drink by age and enter the pit in order; onlookers wept.
units.literal: As wine passed he had young and old go in turn to the pit to receive execution; gentlemen grieved for it.

units.zh: 後唐同光三年三月，詔贈太尉。
units.en: Later Tang Tongguang 3, month 3, he was posthumously named Grand Marshal.
units.literal: In the third month of Later Tang Tongguang year 3, an edict posthumously made him Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 劉知俊，字希賢，徐州沛縣人也。
units.en: Liu Zhijun, courtesy name Xixian, came from Pei in Xuzhou.
units.literal: Liu Zhijun, style name Xixian, was a native of Pei county in Xuzhou.

units.zh: 姿貌雄傑，倜儻有大志。
units.en: He looked heroic, was bold, and dreamed large.
units.literal: His bearing was heroic; he was unconventional and had great ambition.

units.zh: 始事徐帥時溥，為列校，溥甚器之，後以勇略見忌。
units.en: He served Pu as a field officer, was favored, then feared for his prowess.
units.literal: He first served Xu commander Shi Pu as a column officer; Pu greatly valued him, but later because of courage and stratagem was viewed with suspicion.

units.zh: 唐大順二年冬，率所部二千人來降，即署為軍校。
units.en: Datong 2 winter he defected with two thousand men and became an army officer.
units.literal: In winter of the second year of Tang Datong, he led his two thousand men to surrender and was appointed army officer.

units.zh: 知俊披甲上馬，輪劍入敵，勇冠諸將。
units.en: Armored on horseback he charged ahead of every general.
units.literal: Zhijun donned armor, mounted, wheeled his sword into the enemy—his courage topped all generals.

units.zh: 太祖命左右義勝兩軍隸之，尋用為左開道指揮使，故當時人謂之「劉開道」。
units.en: The Founder gave him the Righteous Victory and Victory corps; he became Left Vanguard commander and was called "Liu Vanguard."
units.literal: The Founder assigned the Righteous Victory and Victory armies to him; soon he was used as Left Vanguard commander, so people of the time called him "Liu Vanguard."

units.zh: 後討秦宗權及攻徐州，皆有功，尋補徐州馬步軍都指揮使。
units.en: He fought Zongquan and took Xuzhou, then commanded Xu's horse and foot.
units.literal: Later in attacking Qin Zongquan and assaulting Xuzhou he had merit; soon he was made overall commander of Xu horse and foot.

units.zh: 攻海州下之，遂奏授刺史。
units.en: He captured Haizhou and was made its prefect.
units.literal: In attacking Haizhou he took it and memorialized appointment as prefect.

units.zh: 天復初，曆典懷、鄭二州，從平青州，以功奏授同州節度使。
units.en: Early Tianfu he held Huai and Zheng; pacifying Qing won him Tong commissioner.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he successively governed Huai and Zheng; in pacifying Qingzhou, for merit he was memorialized military commissioner of Tong.

units.zh: 天祐三年冬，以兵五千破岐軍六萬於美原。
units.en: Tianyou 3 winter he routed sixty thousand Qi troops at Meiyuan with five thousand.
units.literal: In winter of Tianyou year 3, with five thousand troops he broke sixty thousand Qi troops at Meiyuan.

units.zh: 自是連克鄜、延等五州，乃加檢校太傅、平章事。
units.en: He then seized five prefectures including Yan and Yan and rose to honorary Grand Tutor and chief minister.
units.literal: From then he took in succession Yan, Yan, and five other prefectures, and was raised to honorary Grand Tutor and co-equal chief minister.

units.zh: 開平二年春三月，命為潞州行營招討使。
units.en: Kaiping 2 spring, month 3, he was named Lu campaign commander.
units.literal: In the third month of spring of Kaiping year 2, he was ordered campaign commander of Lu.

units.zh: 知俊未至潞，夾寨已陷，晉人引軍方攻澤州，聞知俊至，乃退。
units.en: Before he reached Lu the camps had fallen; Jin besieged Zezhou but withdrew when he came.
units.literal: Zhijun had not yet reached Lu when the flanking camps had already fallen; Jin men led troops attacking Zezhou; hearing Zhijun had come, they withdrew.

units.zh: 尋改西路招討使。
units.en: He was soon made western-route campaign commander.
units.literal: Soon he was changed to western-route campaign commander.

units.zh: 六月，大破岐軍於幕穀，俘斬千計，李茂貞僅以身免。
units.en: Month 6 he crushed Qi at Mugul, killing thousands; Maozhen barely escaped.
units.literal: In the sixth month he greatly defeated Qi troops at Mugul, capturing and beheading a thousand-odd; Li Maozhen barely escaped with his body.

units.zh: 三年五月，加檢校太尉、兼侍中，封大彭郡王。
units.en: In the fifth month of the third year, he became honorary Grand Marshal, Palace Secretary, and Prince of Dapeng.
units.literal: In the fifth month of year 3 he was raised to honorary Grand Marshal and concurrent Palace Secretary, enfeoffed Prince of Dapeng.

units.zh: 時知俊威望益隆，太祖雄猜日甚，會佑國軍節度使王重師無罪見誅，知俊居不自安，乃據同州叛，
units.en: Zhijun's fame grew while the Founder grew suspicious; when innocent Wang Chongshi was killed, Zhijun rebelled at Tong,
units.literal: At that time Zhijun's prestige daily grew; the Founder's suspicious nature daily deepened; when Youguo military commissioner Wang Chongshi was executed without crime, Zhijun could not rest easy in his place and then held Tong in rebellion,

units.zh: 〈（《鑒戒錄》云：彭城王劉知俊鎮同州日，因築營牆，掘得一物，重八十餘斤，狀若油囊，召賓幕將校問之。
units.en: (The 《Mirror of Warning》 says that while fortifying Tong, Zhijun unearthed an eighty-jin object like an oil bladder and asked his staff.
units.literal: (The 《Mirror of Warning》 says: When Prince of Pengcheng Liu Zhijun was at Tong and built camp walls, he dug up an object weighing more than eighty jin, shaped like an oil bladder, and summoned guests and officers to ask about it.

units.zh: 劉源曰：「此是冤氣所結，古來囹圄之地或有焉。
units.en: Liu Yuan said, "This was condensed grievance from an old prison site.
units.literal: Liu Yuan said: "This is grievance-qi congealed; in ancient prison grounds there sometimes is such.

units.zh: 昔王充據洛陽，修河南府獄，亦獲此物。
units.en: Wang Chong had found the same when rebuilding Luoyang's jail.
units.literal: Formerly when Wang Chong held Luoyang and repaired the Henan prefectural prison, this object was also obtained.

units.zh: 源聞酒能忘憂，奠以醇醪，或可消釋耳。
units.en: Wine might dissolve it, Yuan said.
units.literal: Yuan heard wine can make one forget sorrow; offering pure wine might dissolve it.

units.zh: 然此物之出，亦非吉征也。」
units.en: Still, he added, the omen was ill."
units.literal: Yet the appearance of this object is also not an auspicious sign.

units.zh: 知俊命具酒饌祝酹，復瘞之。
units.en: Zhijun poured wine, prayed, and reburied it.
units.literal: Zhijun ordered wine and food prepared for libation, and reburied it.

units.zh: 尋有叛城背主之事。）〉
units.en: Soon he rebelled.)〉
units.literal: Soon there was the matter of rebelling and betraying the lord.)〉

units.zh: 送款於李茂貞。
units.en: He submitted to Li Maozhen.
units.literal: He sent allegiance to Li Maozhen.

units.zh: 又分兵以襲雍、華，雍州節度使劉捍被擒，送鳳翔害之，華州蔡敬思被傷獲免。
units.en: He raided Yong and Hua; Liu Han was taken to Fengxiang and killed; Cai Jingsi was wounded but lived.
units.literal: He also divided troops to strike Yong and Hua; Yong military commissioner Liu Han was captured and sent to Fengxiang to be killed; Hua's Cai Jingsi was wounded but escaped.

units.zh: 太祖聞知俊叛，遣近臣諭之曰：「朕待卿甚厚，何相負耶？」
units.en: The Founder asked, "I favored you—why betray me?"
units.literal: The Founder, hearing Zhijun had rebelled, sent a close attendant to instruct him: "I treated you very generously—why have you failed me?"

units.zh: 知俊報曰：「臣非背德，但畏死耳！
units.en: Zhijun answered, "I do not betray you—I fear death!
units.literal: Zhijun replied: "Your subject does not betray virtue, but only fears death!

units.zh: 王重師不負陛下，而致族滅！」
units.en: Chongshi was loyal, yet you wiped out his house!"
units.literal: Wang Chongshi did not fail Your Majesty, yet his clan was destroyed!"

units.zh: 太祖復遣使謂知俊曰：「朕不料卿為此。
units.en: The Founder said, "I never expected this of you.
units.literal: The Founder again sent an envoy telling Zhijun: "I did not expect you would do this.

units.zh: 昨重師得罪，蓋劉捍言陰結邠、鳳，終不為國家用。
units.en: Chongshi died because Han claimed he plotted with Bin and Feng and would never serve the throne.
units.literal: Yesterday Chongshi's crime—because Liu Han said he secretly linked with Bin and Feng and in the end would not serve the state's use.

units.zh: 我今雖知枉濫，悔不可追，致卿如斯，我心恨恨，蓋劉捍誤予事也，捍一死固未塞責。」
units.en: I know it was unjust and cannot undo it; Han misled me—his death is not enough."
units.literal: Today though I know it was excessive punishment, regret cannot be undone; causing you to be like this, my heart hates it—the fault lies with Liu Han misleading me in the affair; Han's one death truly does not answer the blame."

units.zh: 知俊不報，遂分兵以守潼關。
units.en: Zhijun was silent and garrisoned Tong Pass.
units.literal: Zhijun did not reply and then divided troops to guard Tong Pass.

units.zh: 太祖命劉鄩率兵進討，攻潼關，下之。
units.en: The Founder sent Liu Ye, who took Tong Pass.
units.literal: The Founder ordered Liu Ye to lead troops in pursuit, attacked Tong Pass, and took it.

units.zh: 時知俊弟知浣為親衛指揮使，聞知俊叛，自洛奔至潼關，為鄩所擒，害之。
units.en: His brother Zhihuan fled from Luoyang to Tong Pass, was caught by Ye, and killed.
units.literal: At that time Zhijun's younger brother Zhihuan was personal guard commander; hearing Zhijun had rebelled, he fled from Luo to Tong Pass, was seized by Ye, and killed.

units.zh: 尋而王師繼至，知俊乃舉族奔於鳳翔；
units.en: Wang's army followed; Zhijun fled with his clan to Fengxiang;
units.literal: Soon Wang's army followed; Zhijun then led his whole clan to flee to Fengxiang;

units.zh: 李茂貞厚待之，偽加檢校太尉、兼中書令，以土疆不廣，無藩鎮以處之，但厚給俸祿而已。
units.en: Maozhen honored him with empty titles but no domain, only rich pay.
units.literal: Li Maozhen treated him generously, falsely raised him to honorary Grand Marshal and concurrent Grand Secretary; because territory was not broad there was no frontier post to place him in, but only rich salary was given.

units.zh: 尋命率兵攻圍靈武，且圖牧圉之地。
units.en: He was sent to besiege Lingwu and seize pasture.
units.literal: Soon he was ordered to lead troops to besiege Lingwu and also plan pasture lands.

units.zh: 靈武節度使韓遜遣使來告急，太祖令康懷英率師救之，師次邠州長城嶺，為知俊邀擊，懷英敗歸。
units.en: Han Xun of Lingwu begged aid; Kang Huaiying marched, was ambushed at Changcheng Ridge, and retreated.
units.literal: Lingwu military commissioner Han Xun sent an envoy in urgent appeal; the Founder ordered Kang Huaiying to lead troops to rescue; the army reached Changcheng Ridge in Bin prefecture and was intercepted by Zhijun; Huaiying was defeated and returned.

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》云：李彥琦、劉知俊自靈武班師，塗經長城嶺，梁師率精銳數萬躡其後，彥琦與知俊同設方略，擊敗之。）〉
units.en: (The 《Record of the Nine States》 says Yanqi and Zhijun, returning from Lingwu, beat a Liang pursuit at Changcheng Ridge.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Record of the Nine States》 says: Li Yanqi and Liu Zhijun, returning from Lingwu, passed Changcheng Ridge; Liang troops with tens of thousands of elite followed; Yanqi and Zhijun together devised strategy and defeated them.)〉

units.zh: 茂貞悅，署為涇州節度使。
units.en: Maozhen made him Jing commissioner.
units.literal: Maozhen was pleased and appointed him Jing military commissioner.

units.zh: 復命率眾攻興元，進圍西縣，會蜀軍救至，乃退。
units.en: He besieged Xixian at Xingyuan until Shu relief forced retreat.
units.literal: Again he was ordered to lead the masses to attack Xingyuan, advanced to besiege Xixian; when Shu troops came to rescue, he withdrew.

units.zh: 〈（《九國誌·王宗鐬傳》云：岐將劉知俊等領大軍分路來攻，由階、成路奪固鎮糧，王宗侃、唐襲等禦之，至青泥嶺，為知俊所敗，退保西縣。
units.en: (The 《Record of the Nine States · Wang Zonghe》 says Zhijun routed Shu forces at Qingni and besieged Xixian.
units.literal: (The 《Record of the Nine States · Biography of Wang Zonghe》 says: Qi generals Liu Zhijun and others led a great army by separate routes to attack; by the Jie and Cheng road they seized Guzhen grain; Wang Zongkan and Tang Xi and others met them; reaching Qingni Ridge they were defeated by Zhijun and retreated to hold Xixian.

units.zh: 會大雨，漢江漲，宗鐬自羅村得鄉導，緣山而行數百里，與宗播遇於鐵穀，合軍出湯頭。
units.en: Rain flooded the Han; Zonghe marched by mountain paths and joined Zongbo at Tiegul.
units.literal: Meeting great rain, the Han River rose; Zonghe from Luocun got a village guide, followed the mountains several hundred li, and met Zongbo at Tiegul; united armies came out at Tangtou.

units.zh: 時知俊自斜穀山南直抵興州，圍西縣，軍人散掠巴中，宗鐬與宗播襲之。
units.en: Zhijun swept down from Xiegu, besieged Xixian, and looted Ba until Zonghe and Zongbo struck.
units.literal: At that time Zhijun from Xiegu Mountain south went straight to Xing prefecture, besieged Xixian; soldiers scattered to plunder Ba; Zonghe and Zongbo struck them.

units.zh: 會王建亦至，遂解西縣之圍。）〉
units.en: Wang Jian arrived and lifted the siege.)〉
units.literal: When Wang Jian also arrived, the siege of Xixian was then lifted.)〉

units.zh: 既而為茂貞左右石簡顒等間之，免其軍政，寓於岐下，掩關曆年。
units.en: Courtiers slandered him; he lived under Qi in seclusion for years.
units.literal: Soon he was set aside from military government by Maozhen's close associates Shi Jian'e and others; he dwelt under Qi, shutting his gate for years.

units.zh: 茂貞猶子繼崇鎮秦州，因來寧覲，言知俊途窮至此，不宜以讒嫉見疑，茂貞乃誅簡顒等以安其心。
units.en: Nephew Jichong pleaded for Zhijun; Maozhen executed the slanderers to reassure him.
units.literal: Maozhen's nephew Jichong governed Qin prefecture; coming to pay respects he said Zhijun, driven to extremity, should not be suspected through slander; Maozhen then executed Jian'e and others to calm his heart.

units.zh: 繼崇又請令知俊挈家居秦州，以就豐給，茂貞從之。
units.en: Jichong invited Zhijun's family to Qin; Maozhen agreed.
units.literal: Jichong again asked that Zhijun be allowed to bring his household to live at Qin to enjoy abundance; Maozhen consented.

units.zh: 未幾，邠州亂，茂貞命知俊討之。
units.en: Bin rebelled; Maozhen sent Zhijun to suppress it.
units.literal: Before long, Bin prefecture rebelled; Maozhen ordered Zhijun to suppress it.

units.zh: 時邠州都校李保衡納款於朝廷，末帝遣霍彥威率眾先入於邠，知俊遂圍其城，半載不能下。
units.en: Li Baoheng had surrendered to Liang; Huo Yanwei entered Bin first; Zhijun besieged it six months in vain.
units.literal: At that time Bin's commander Li Baoheng had submitted to the court; the Last Emperor sent Huo Yanwei with troops to enter Bin first; Zhijun then besieged the city; half a year could not take it.

units.zh: 會李繼崇以秦州降於蜀，知俊妻孥皆遷於成都，遂解邠州之圍而歸岐陽。
units.en: Jichong surrendered Qin to Shu; Zhijun's family was taken to Chengdu; he abandoned Bin and returned to Qiyang.
units.literal: When Li Jichong surrendered Qin to Shu, Zhijun's wife and children were all moved to Chengdu; he then lifted the siege of Bin and returned to Qiyang.

units.zh: 以舉家入蜀，終慮猜忌，因與親信百餘人夜斬關奔蜀。
units.en: Fearing suspicion after his family went to Shu, he fled by night with a hundred men.
units.literal: Because his whole household had entered Shu, he finally feared suspicion; with more than a hundred trusted men he cut the pass by night and fled to Shu.

units.zh: 王建待之甚至，即授偽武信軍節度使，尋命將兵伐岐，不克，班師，因圍隴州，獲其帥桑宏誌以歸。
units.en: Wang Jian honored him as Wuxin commissioner; he failed against Qi, took Long and Sang Hongzhi, and returned.
units.literal: Wang Jian treated him to the utmost; he was at once made false Wuxin military commissioner; soon he was ordered to lead troops against Qi without success and withdrew; then he besieged Long prefecture, took its commander Sang Hongzhi, and returned.

units.zh: 久之，復命為都統，再領軍伐岐。
units.en: Later he was made overall commander and marched on Qi again.
units.literal: After a long time he was again ordered as overall commander and again led troops against Qi.

units.zh: 時部將皆王建舊人，多違節度，不成功而還，蜀人因而毀之。
units.en: At the time his subordinate generals were all Wang Jian's old men and mostly disobeyed command; they returned without success, and the Shu people slandered him for it.
units.literal: At that time the subordinate generals were all Wang Jian's old men and mostly disobeyed command; they did not succeed and returned; Shu men therefore slandered him.

units.zh: 先是，王建雖加寵待，然亦忌之，嘗謂近侍曰：「吾漸衰耗，恒思身後。
units.en: Jian favored yet feared him and told aides, "I age and think of what follows my death.
units.literal: Earlier, though Wang Jian added favor and treatment, he also was jealous; he once told close attendants: "I gradually decline and constantly think of after my death.

units.zh: 劉知俊非爾輩能駕馭，不如早為之所。」
units.en: Zhijun is not for you to control—deal with him early."
units.literal: Liu Zhijun is not what you can drive and rein—better early do something about him."

units.zh: 又嫉其名者於裏巷間作謠言云：「黑牛出圈棕繩斷。」
units.en: Enemies spread a rhyme: "The black ox leaves the pen; the palm rope snaps."
units.literal: Those who envied his name also made a street song in the lanes: "The black ox leaves the pen; the palm rope breaks."

units.zh: 知俊色黔而醜生，棕繩者，王氏子孫皆以「宗」、「承」為名，故以此構之。
units.en: Zhijun was dark and ugly; "palm rope" punned on Wang names using Zong and Cheng.
units.literal: Zhijun's complexion was dark and he was born ugly; "palm rope" means Wang's sons and grandsons all used "Zong" and "Cheng" in their names—thus they framed him with this.

units.zh: 偽蜀天漢元年冬十二月，建遣人捕知俊，斬於成都府之炭市。
units.en: False-Shu Tianhan 1, month 12, Jian had him beheaded at Chengdu's charcoal market.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of winter of false-Shu Tianhan year 1, Jian sent men to seize Zhijun and behead him at the charcoal market of Chengdu prefecture.

units.zh: 及王衍嗣偽位，以其子嗣禋尚偽峨眉長公主，拜駙馬都尉。
units.en: Under Wang Yan his son Sichen married the Emei princess and became chief son-in-law.
units.literal: When Wang Yan succeeded the false throne, his son Sichen married the false Emei senior princess and was appointed Chief Son-in-law.

units.zh: 後唐同光末，隨例遷於洛，卒。
units.en: At Later Tang Tongguang he moved to Luoyang and died.
units.literal: At the end of Later Tang Tongguang, following precedent he moved to Luo and died.

units.zh: 知俊族子嗣彬，幼從知俊征行，累遷為軍校。
units.en: Clansman Sizhen campaigned with Zhijun and rose to field officer.
units.literal: Zhijun's clansman nephew Sizhen, in youth followed Zhijun on campaign, was repeatedly promoted to army officer.

units.zh: 及知俊叛，以不預其謀，得不坐。
units.en: He was not punished when Zhijun rebelled.
units.literal: When Zhijun rebelled, because he did not share the plot he was not implicated.

units.zh: 貞明末，大軍與晉王對壘於德勝，久之，嗣彬率數騎奔於晉，具言朝廷軍機得失；
units.en: At Zhenming's end, with Jin at Desheng, Sizhen defected with horsemen and revealed Liang plans;
units.literal: At the end of Zhenming, the great army and the Prince of Jin faced each other at Desheng a long time; soon Sizhen with several riders fled to Jin and fully told the court army's gains and losses in military affairs;

units.zh: 又以家世仇怨，將以報之。
units.en: He sought to avenge a family feud.
units.literal: Also because of family hatred through generations, he would repay it.

units.zh: 晉王深信之，即厚給田宅，仍賜錦衣玉帶，軍中目為「劉二哥」。
units.en: The Prince of Jin trusted him, gave estates and the jade belt, and called him "Second Brother Liu."
units.literal: The Prince of Jin deeply trusted him, immediately gave rich fields and houses, and also bestowed brocade robes and jade belt; in the army they called him "Second Brother Liu."

units.zh: 居一年，復來奔，當時晉人謂是刺客，以晉王恩澤之厚，故不竊發。
units.en: A year later he fled back; Jin suspected an assassin but spared him for past favor.
units.literal: After a year he came fleeing back; at that time Jin men said he was an assassin; because the Prince of Jin's grace was so thick, he did not strike secretly.

units.zh: 龍德三年冬，從王彥章戰於中都，軍敗，為晉人所擒。
units.en: Longde 3 winter he fought at Zhongdu, was captured.
units.literal: In winter of Longde year 3 he followed Wang Yanzhang in battle at Zhongdu; the army was defeated and he was seized by Jin men.

units.zh: 晉王見之，笑謂嗣彬曰：「爾可還予玉帶。」
units.en: The Prince of Jin smiled and told Sizhen, "Return my jade belt."
units.literal: The Prince of Jin saw him and smiling told Sizhen: "You may return my jade belt to me."

units.zh: 嗣彬惶恐請死，遂誅之。
units.en: Sizhen begged death and was executed.
units.literal: Sizhen in fear begged death and was then executed.

units.zh: 楊崇本，不知何許人，幼為李茂貞之假子，因冒姓李氏，名繼徽。
units.en: Yang Chongben, origin unknown, was adopted by Li Maozhen and took the name Li Jihui.
units.literal: Yang Chongben—unknown where a native—in youth became Li Maozhen's adopted son, and therefore usurped the surname Li, name Jihui.

units.zh: 唐光化中，茂貞表為邠州節度使。
units.en: In Guanghua Maozhen made him Bin commissioner.
units.literal: In Guanghua of Tang he was memorialized as Bin military commissioner.

units.zh: 天復元年冬，太祖自鳳翔移軍北伐，駐旆於邠郊，命諸軍攻其城。
units.en: Tianfu 1 winter the Founder left Fengxiang, camped at Bin, and assaulted the walls.
units.literal: In winter of Tianfu year 1, the Founder moved the army from Fengxiang north to campaign, halted banners at Bin's suburbs, and ordered the armies to attack the city.

units.zh: 崇本懼，出城請降。
units.en: Chongben surrendered in fear.
units.literal: Chongben in fear went out of the city and begged surrender.

units.zh: 太祖復置為邠州節度使，仍令復其本姓名焉。
units.en: The Founder restored him as Bin commissioner under his true name Yang Chongben.
units.literal: The Founder again installed him as Bin military commissioner and still ordered restoration of his original surname and given name.

units.zh: 及師還，遷其族於河中。
units.en: On withdrawal his clan was moved to Hezhong.
units.literal: When the army returned, his clan was moved to Hezhong.

units.zh: 其後，太祖因統戎往來由於蒲津，以崇本妻素有姿色，嬖之於別館。
units.en: The Founder, passing Pujin on campaign, took Chongben's beautiful wife to a side lodge.
units.literal: Afterward, because the Founder in commanding troops came and went by Pujin, he kept Chongben's wife, who had always had beauty, as a favorite in a separate lodge.

units.zh: 其婦素剛烈，私懷愧恥，遣侍者讓崇本曰：「丈夫擁旄仗鉞，不能庇其伉儷，我已為朱公婦，今生無面目對卿，期於刀繩而已。」
units.en: His wife was by nature fierce and strong, and privately bore shame. She sent an attendant to reproach Chongben: "A husband who holds banners and axes yet cannot shelter his wife! I have already become Master Zhu's woman; in this life I have no face to meet you. Only the knife or the cord remains."
units.literal: His wife was by nature fierce and strong; privately she bore shame; she sent an attendant to reproach Chongben: "A husband holding banners and axes cannot shelter his wife—I have already become Master Zhu's woman; in this life I have no face to meet you—only the knife and cord remain."

units.zh: 崇本聞之，但灑淚含怒。
units.en: Chongben wept in silent rage.
units.literal: Chongben heard it and only shed tears containing anger.

units.zh: 及昭宗自鳳翔回京，崇本之家得歸邠州。
units.en: When Zhaozong returned from Fengxiang, his household came back to Bin.
units.literal: When Zhaozong returned from Fengxiang to the capital, Chongben's household was able to return to Bin prefecture.

units.zh: 崇本恥其妻見辱，因茲復貳於太祖。
units.en: Humiliated, he turned against the Founder again.
units.literal: Chongben, shamed that his wife had been insulted, from this again turned against the Founder.

units.zh: 乃遣使告茂貞曰：「朱氏兆亂，謀危唐祚，父為國家磐石，不可坐觀其禍，宜於此時畢命興復，事苟不濟，死為社稷可也。」
units.en: He told Maozhen, "Zhu threatens Tang; you are the realm's pillar—rise now or die for the altars."
units.literal: He then sent an envoy telling Maozhen: "The Zhu clan foretells disorder and plots danger to Tang's mandate; father, as the state's bedrock, cannot sit and watch the calamity; at this time you should stake life on restoration; if the affair does not succeed, dying for the altars is also fitting."

units.zh: 茂貞乃遣使會兵於太原。
units.en: Maozhen allied with Taiyuan.
units.literal: Maozhen then sent envoys to join troops at Taiyuan.

units.zh: 時西川王建亦令大將出師以助之，岐、蜀連兵以攻雍、華，關西大震。
units.en: Wang Jian of Shu marched out; Qi and Shu struck Yong and Hua and shook the northwest.
units.literal: At that time western Sichuan's Wang Jian also ordered a great general to march out to aid; Qi and Shu joined armies to attack Yong and Hua; west of the passes shook greatly.

units.zh: 太祖遣郴王友裕帥師禦之，會友裕卒於行，乃班師。
units.en: The Founder sent Prince of Chen Youyu; when Youyu died on the march, the army withdrew.
units.literal: The Founder sent Prince of Chen Youyu to command troops against them; when Youyu died on campaign, the army withdrew.

units.zh: 天祐三年冬十月，崇本復領鳳翔、邠、涇、秦、隴之師，會延州胡章之眾，合五六萬，屯於美原，列柵十五，其勢甚盛。
units.en: Tianyou 3, month 10, Chongben massed fifty or sixty thousand at Meiyuan in fifteen camps.
units.literal: In the tenth month of winter of Tianyou year 3, Chongben again led Fengxiang, Bin, Jing, Qin, and Long armies, joined with Yanzhou Hu Zhang's masses, five or six ten-thousands in all, camped at Meiyuan, set fifteen palisades in array—their momentum very strong.

units.zh: 太祖命同州節度使劉知俊及康懷英帥師拒之，崇本大敗，復歸於邠州，自是垂翅久之。
units.en: The Founder ordered Liu Zhijun, military governor of Tong Prefecture, and Kang Huaiying to lead troops against him. Chongben was badly defeated, returned to Bin Prefecture, and thereafter lay low for a long time.
units.literal: The Founder ordered Tong military commissioner Liu Zhijun and Kang Huaiying to command troops against them; Chongben was greatly defeated, returned to Bin, and from then hung his wings a long time.

units.zh: 乾化元年冬，為其子彥魯所毒而死。
units.en: Qianhua 1 winter his son Yanlu poisoned him.
units.literal: In winter of Qianhua year 1, he was poisoned to death by his son Yanlu.

units.zh: 彥魯自稱留後，領其軍事，凡五十餘日，為崇本養子李保衡所殺。
units.en: Yanlu seized power for fifty days until adopted son Li Baoheng killed him.
units.literal: Yanlu declared himself acting commissioner and held military affairs; for fifty-odd days he was killed by Chongben's adopted son Li Baoheng.

units.zh: 保衡舉其城來降，末帝命霍彥威為邠帥，由是邠、寧復為末帝所有。
units.en: Baoheng surrendered the city; the Last Emperor named Huo Yanwei Bin commander and recovered Bin and Ning.
units.literal: Baoheng raised his city to surrender; the Last Emperor appointed Huo Yanwei as Bin commander; thereby Bin and Ning again belonged to the Last Emperor.

units.zh: 蔣殷，不知何許人。
units.en: Baoheng surrendered; the Last Emperor made Huo Yanwei Bin commander and recovered Bin and Ning.
units.literal: Baoheng offered the city in surrender; the Last Emperor ordered Huo Yanwei as Bin commander; from then Bin and Ning again belonged to the Last Emperor.

units.zh: 幼孤，隨其母適於河中節度使王重盈之家，重盈憐之，畜為己子。
units.en: Jiang Yin's origin is unknown.
units.literal: Jiang Yin—unknown where a native.

units.zh: 唐天復初，太祖既平蒲、陝，殷與從兄珂舉族遷於大梁。
units.en: Orphaned, he was raised in Wang Chongying's house at Hezhong.
units.literal: Orphaned in youth, he followed his mother into the household of Hezhong military commissioner Wang Chongying; Chongying pitied him and raised him as his own son.

units.zh: 太祖感王重榮之舊恩，凡王氏諸子，皆錄用焉，殷由是繼曆內職，累遷至宣徽院使。
units.en: Early Tianfu, after Pu and Shan fell, Yin and cousin Ke moved to Daliang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tang Tianfu, after the Founder had pacified Pu and Shan, Yin and his cousin Ke moved their whole clan to Daliang.

units.zh: 殷素與庶人友珪善，友珪篡立，命為徐州節度使。
units.en: Remembering Wang Chongrong, the Founder employed the Wang sons; Yin rose to Palace Proclamation commissioner.
units.literal: The Founder, moved by Wang Chongrong's old grace, recorded and employed all the Wang sons; Yin by this successively held inner posts, rising to Palace Proclamation commissioner.

units.zh: 乾化四年秋，末帝以福王友璋鎮徐方，殷自以為友珪之黨，懼不受代，遂堅壁以拒命。
units.en: Close to Yougui, he was made Xu commissioner when Yougui usurped.
units.literal: Yin had always been friendly with the commoner Yougui; when Yougui usurped the throne he was ordered Xuzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 時華州節度使王瓚，殷之從弟也，懼其連坐，上章言殷本姓蔣，非王氏之子也。
units.en: Cousin Wang Zan of Hua, fearing guilt, revealed Yin was born Jiang, not Wang.
units.literal: At that time Hua military commissioner Wang Zan was Yin's cousin and feared being implicated; he memorialized that Yin's original surname was Jiang, not a Wang son.

units.zh: 末帝乃下詔削奪殷在身官爵，仍令卻還本姓，命牛存節、劉鄩等率軍討之。
units.en: The court stripped his titles, restored the surname Jiang, and sent Niu Cunjie and Liu Ye against him.
units.literal: The Last Emperor then issued an edict stripping Yin of office and rank in his person, still ordering return to his original surname, and ordered Niu Cunjie, Liu Ye, and others to lead troops against him.

units.zh: 是時，殷求救於淮南，楊溥遣朱瑾率眾來援，存節等逆擊，敗之。
units.en: He begged Huainan; Yang Pu sent Zhu Jin; Cunjie defeated Jin.
units.literal: At that time Yin sought rescue from Huainan; Yang Pu sent Zhu Jin with masses to aid; Cunjie and the rest met and defeated them.

units.zh: 貞明元年春，存節、劉鄩攻下徐州，殷舉族自燔而死，於火中得其屍，梟首以獻之。
units.en: In spring of Zhenming 1, Cunjie and Liu Xun captured Xu Prefecture. Yin and his whole clan burned themselves to death; his corpse was recovered from the fire, and his head was cut off and presented.
units.literal: In spring of Zhenming year 1, Cunjie and Liu Ye took Xuzhou; Yin and his whole clan burned themselves to death; from the fire his corpse was obtained, the head cut off and presented.

units.zh: 張萬進，雲州人。
units.en: Zhang Wanjin came from Yunzhou.
units.literal: Zhang Wanjin was a man of Yun prefecture.

units.zh: 初為本州小校，亡命投幽州，劉守光厚遇之，任為裨將。
units.en: Originally a junior officer in his own prefecture, he fled to Youzhou and served Liu Shouguang as lieutenant.
units.literal: At first he was a junior officer of his prefecture; he fled and threw himself on Youzhou; Liu Shouguang treated him generously and used him as a lieutenant.

units.zh: 滄州劉守文，以弟守光囚父而竊據其位，自領兵問罪，尋敗於雞蘇。
units.en: Liu Shouwen of Cangzhou marched against Shouguang, who had imprisoned their father; Shouwen lost at Jisu.
units.literal: Cangzhou's Liu Shouwen, because his younger brother Shouguang imprisoned their father and usurped the post, himself led troops to demand justice; soon he was defeated at Jisu.

units.zh: 守光遂兼有滄、景之地，令其子繼威主留務。
units.en: Shouguang took Cang and Jing and left son Jiwei in charge.
units.literal: Shouguang then combined Cang and Jing territory and ordered his son Jiwei to hold acting affairs.

units.zh: 繼威年幼，未能政事，以萬進佐之，凡關軍政，一皆委任。
units.en: Young Jiwei delegated all military affairs to Wanjin.
units.literal: Jiwei was young and could not manage government; he had Wanjin assist him; all military government was entirely entrusted.

units.zh: 繼威凶虐類父，嘗淫亂於萬進之家，萬進怒而殺之，
units.en: Jiwei raped Wanjin's household; Wanjin killed him,
units.literal: Jiwei was cruel and violent like his father; he once committed lewdness in Wanjin's house; Wanjin in anger killed him,

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：乾化二年九月庚子，萬進遣使奉表降於梁。
units.en: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 records that in Qianhua 2, month 9, day gengzi, Wanjin surrendered to Liang.
units.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: On gengzi day of the ninth month of Qianhua year 2, Wanjin sent an envoy presenting a memorial surrendering to Liang.

units.zh: 辛丑，以萬進為義昌留後。
units.en: On day xinchou he became Yichang acting commissioner.
units.literal: On xinchou day he was made Yichang acting commissioner.

units.zh: 甲辰，改義昌為順化軍，以萬進為節度使。
units.en: On day jiachen Yichang became Shunhua army under Wanjin as commissioner.
units.literal: On jiachen day Yichang was changed to Shunhua army; Wanjin was made military commissioner.

units.zh: 此傳疑有闕文。）〉
units.en: This passage may be incomplete.)〉
units.literal: This biography perhaps has missing text.)〉

units.zh: 師厚表青州節度使，俄遷兗州，仍賜名守進。
units.en: Shihou made him Qing commissioner, then Yan, with the name Shoujin.
units.literal: Shihou memorialized him Qingzhou military commissioner; soon he was transferred to Yanzhou, and still was granted the name Shoujin.

units.zh: 萬進性既輕險，專圖反側。
units.en: Wanjin was treacherous and lived for revolt.
units.literal: Wanjin's nature was light and dangerous; he specialized in plotting rebellion.

units.zh: 貞明四年冬，據城叛命，遣使送款於晉王。
units.en: Zhenming 4 winter he rebelled and submitted to the Prince of Jin.
units.literal: In winter of Zhenming year 4, he held the city in rebellion, sent envoys with allegiance to the Prince of Jin.

units.zh: 末帝降製削其官爵，仍復其本名，遣劉鄩討之，晉人不能救。
units.en: The Last Emperor stripped his titles, restored his name Zhang, and sent Liu Ye; Jin could not save him.
units.literal: The Last Emperor by edict stripped his office and rank, still restored his original name, and sent Liu Ye to attack; Jin men could not rescue.

units.zh: 五年冬，萬進危蹙，小將邢師遇潛謀內應，開門以納王師，遂拔其城，萬進族誅。
units.en: Year 5 winter, desperate, he was betrayed when Xing Shiyu opened the gates; his clan was wiped out.
units.literal: In winter of year 5, Wanjin was in desperate straits; petty officer Xing Shiyu secretly plotted internal response, opened the gate to admit the royal army, and then took the city; Wanjin's clan was exterminated.

units.zh: 史臣曰：夫雲雷構屯，龍蛇起陸，勢均者交鬥，力敗者先亡，故瑄、瑾、時溥之流，皆梁之吞噬，斯亦理之常也。
units.en: The historian writes: When storm clouds gather and serpents rise, equals fight until the weaker is devoured—Xuan, Jin, and Shi Pu were Liang's prey, as reason demands.
units.literal: The historian says: When cloud and thunder build in hardship and dragons and serpents rise on land, equals contend in battle and the defeated perish first—thus the stream of Xuan, Jin, and Shi Pu were all swallowed by Liang; this too is reason's constant.

units.zh: 惟瑾始以竊發有土，終以竊發亡身，《傳》所謂「君以此始，必以此終」者乎！
units.en: Only Jin stole a realm by stealth and lost his life the same way—is this not what the 《Classic》 calls "with this you begin, with this you end"?
units.literal: Only Jin began by stealth and gained territory, ended by stealth and lost his person—is this not what the 《Classic》 calls "with this you begin, with this you end"?

units.zh: 師範屬衰季之運，以興復為謀，事雖不成，忠則可尚，雖貽族滅之禍，亦可以與臧洪遊於地下矣。
units.en: Shifan, in a dying age, sought restoration; though he failed and his house was killed, his loyalty ranks with Zang Hong.
units.literal: Shifan belonged to a declining age's fortune yet plotted restoration; though the affair did not succeed, loyalty may be honored—though he suffered clan extermination, he may wander underground with Zang Hong.

units.zh: 知俊驍武有餘，奔亡不暇，六合雖大，無所容身，夫如是則豈若義以為勇者乎！
units.en: Zhijun's valor availed nothing in endless flight; the world had no room for him—better courage rooted in duty.
units.literal: Zhijun had martial valor to spare yet fled without rest; though the six directions are broad, nowhere could contain his body—would it not be better to make righteousness the courage?

units.zh: 崇本而下，俱以叛滅，又何足以道哉！
units.en: Chongben and the rest died as rebels and merit no further words!
units.literal: Chongben and those below all perished by rebellion—what is there worth speaking of!

Same mother does not imply same birth year. Later allusions are not personal activity. Research or record a blocker rather than invent precision. A report cannot approve with missing checks or unresolved research.
